blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Managing lead times and cycle times well means measuring them honestly and then attacking them systematically. Many teams still rely on rough averages — "it takes about three weeks" — without realising that their real lead time is a mixture: 60% of orders at two weeks, 30% at four weeks, and 10% at six. The average hides everything that matters.

The fix is to measure the distribution, not just the average. What is the 95th percentile? What is the worst-case? Which steps add the most variation? Once you can see that, improvement becomes focused. You attack the widest gap, the slowest step, the biggest source of variability — not a vague "be faster".

Good lead-time management over a year can shave weeks off the customer experience without adding a single person to the payroll. That is pure efficiency — and it almost always comes from data, not from effort.

items.q: According to the text, what is the problem with using a rough average?
options: It is only useful for small teams
items.why: "The average hides everything that matters" — a média esconde a variação real.

items.q: What does the text recommend measuring instead of the average?
options: The number of orders per day
items.why: "The fix is to measure the distribution, not just the average."

items.q: According to the text, where do lead-time improvements almost always come from?
items.why: "it almost always comes from data, not from effort."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Variation deserves as much attention as speed
Adding staff is the best way to cut lead times
The worst-case matters as much as the typical case
Focused improvement beats a vague push to be faster
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz que ganhos vêm de dados sem adicionar ninguém à folha — logo, contratar não é o caminho central.

items.q: The example "60% at two weeks, 30% at four, and 10% at six" suggests that…
options: the company has no reliable data at all
the six-week orders are the most common
most orders are actually delivered late
the average of "about three weeks" understates some customers' real wait
items.why: Inferência: uma fatia real espera quatro ou seis semanas, então a média amigável esconde o pior caso.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Harry apresentar a análise de três meses. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Thanks, everyone. For three months we tracked every order end to end, and I want to be honest with you: our friendly line of "about three weeks" is not wrong, but it is misleading.

Here is what the distribution actually looks like. Most orders — roughly six in ten — clear in two weeks. About three in ten take four weeks. And one in ten stretches to six. So when a customer hears "three weeks" and then waits five, they don't feel an average. They feel the tail.

The good news is that the tail is not random. Almost all of it comes from two steps: credit approval and the final quality check. If we fix those two, we can bring the 95th percentile down to four weeks and cut the average by about four days — without adding a single person to the payroll.

So my proposal is simple. Let's stop quoting a number we can't stand behind, attack the two slowest steps first, and report the worst-case, not just the average. That is where the efficiency is hiding.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: According to Harry, what is wrong with the line "about three weeks"?
options: It is not wrong, but it is misleading
It was invented by the customers
items.why: "our friendly line of 'about three weeks' is not wrong, but it is misleading."

items.q: What proportion of orders stretches to six weeks?
items.why: "one in ten stretches to six."

items.q: Which two steps does Harry say cause almost all of the tail?
options: Credit approval and the final quality check
items.why: "Almost all of it comes from two steps: credit approval and the final quality check."

items.q: When Harry says customers "feel the tail, not the average," he means that…
options: the slow, worst-case orders shape how customers experience the service
customers prefer a longer quoted time
items.why: Inferência: quem espera cinco semanas sente o pior caso, não a média de três.

items.q: What is Harry's overall attitude in the presentation?
options: Convinced they need to hire more staff
Honest about the problem but confident it can be fixed
items.why: Inferência: ele admite o problema ("be honest") mas propõe um plano concreto sem aumentar a folha.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The 95th percentile was six weeks, even though the average was three." The 95th percentile is…
options: the value below which 95% of cases fall
the exact midpoint of the data
items.why: Percentil 95 = valor abaixo do qual estão 95% dos casos; mostra o quase-pior caso.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "We can't plan reliably while the ___ between our fastest and slowest orders is so wide."
items.why: Variation = variação: a diferença entre os casos, inimiga da entrega confiável.

items.q: "That change let us shave four days off the cycle." To shave here means to…
items.why: To shave = reduzir um pouco de cada vez, cortar dias do ciclo.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "We improved the numbers without adding a single person to the ___."
items.why: Payroll = folha de pagamento; o ganho veio sem contratar ninguém.

items.q: "The distribution showed a long tail of slow orders." A distribution is…
options: the total sum of the values
the way values spread across a range
items.why: Distribution = distribuição: como os valores se espalham, não apenas a média.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões sobre lead time e eficiência. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "If we fix those steps, we can bring the 95th percentile down to four weeks." Down to signals…
options: the target level reached after a reduction
the starting point before the change
items.why: Down to marca o nível-alvo alcançado (chegar a quatro semanas).

items.q: "We cut the average by four days." Here by expresses…
items.why: By expressa o tamanho da redução (quanto foi cortado), não o nível final.

items.q: "None of these small tweaks will move the needle on the six-week orders." This means they will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.

items.q: "Let's zero in on the two slowest steps first." To zero in on means to…
items.why: Zero in on = concentrar a atenção em algo específico.

items.q: "The RH team agreed the plan but never followed through on the quality check." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado; aqui não levaram.
